title: Mixed commutator coefficient of infinitesimal matrix points
statement: Let k be a field, let V be a finite-dimensional k-vector space, and let G be a closed subgroup scheme of GL(V). Using the dual-number rings of [def-sc-dual-numbers], set A=k[\varepsilon,\delta]/(\varepsilon^2,\delta^2). If X,Y\in\operatorname{End}_k(V) satisfy 1+\varepsilon X\in G(k[\varepsilon]/\varepsilon^2) and 1+\delta Y\in G(k[\delta]/\delta^2), then their base changes to A lie in G(A), and the commutator (1+\varepsilon X)(1+\delta Y)(1-\varepsilon X)(1-\delta Y) lies in G(A) and equals 1+\varepsilon\delta(XY-YX). The inclusion k[\eta]/(\eta^2)\hookrightarrow A given by \eta\mapsto\varepsilon\delta therefore shows 1+\eta(XY-YX)\in G(k[\eta]/\eta^2).
